=== note: A/e_116/ed ===
## Emergency department provider note

**Chief complaint:** lip and tongue swelling.

**History.** The patient presented this evening with swelling of the lips and a sense of fullness in the tongue that has progressed over the course of the day. There was no hives, no itching and no wheeze. Swallowing is uncomfortable but they are handling their saliva and speaking in full sentences. They have taken their usual morning medications and have not eaten anything new or been exposed to anything unusual that they can identify. This has not happened before. Allergy list: no known drug allergies.

**Medications.** Their home list includes <ref id="med_lisinopril">lisinopril 10 mg by mouth daily</ref>. Also on the list are metformin 1000 mg twice daily with meals, empagliflozin 10 mg daily, semaglutide 0.5 mg subcutaneously weekly and rosuvastatin 20 mg nightly. These other medications have not yet been reconciled in the department.

**Exam.** Vitals at 18:47: BP 117/70, HR 105, RR 23, T 98.6 F, SpO2 95%. Uncomfortable but alert. There is visible swelling of the upper and lower lips and moderate swelling of the tongue. The voice is slightly muffled. The oropharynx is partially obscured by the tongue, with no stridor at rest. Lungs are clear. There is no rash on the skin.

**ED course.** Because of the swelling around the airway, they were placed on monitoring with the airway team aware. Methylprednisolone 125 mg IV was given once at 19:06. The swelling and the airway are being watched closely.

**Assessment and plan**

1. <ref id="dx_angioedema">Angioedema, ACE inhibitor-associated</ref>. The picture of lip and tongue swelling without hives or itching, in a patient taking an ACE inhibitor, fits this diagnosis. Lisinopril is stopped, and the patient was told: <ref id="med_lisinopril">"Do not take lisinopril or any ACE inhibitor again."</ref> Continue close airway observation and reassess the swelling frequently. Admission for monitoring is planned given the tongue involvement.
2. Other home medications will be reconciled with the admitting team.
